query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of aluminum (Al) to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective oxide layer on the surface.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of aluminum (Al)
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 800-1000 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: 5 hours, loading: no external loading
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer on the surface
generation.mechanism: The added Al reacts with oxygen to form a stable oxide layer, which prevents further oxidation of the underlying material
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance, as evidenced by reduced oxidation and improved mechanical properties after exposure to high temperatures
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 800-1000 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: 5 hours, loading: no external loading
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Al required to achieve optimal oxygen resistance is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Expose untreated and Al-added equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples to air at 800-1000 °C for 5 hours, then measure their mechanical properties and oxidation resistance
measurements: Oxidation resistance (e.g. weight gain, oxide layer thickness)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-added sample shows no significant improvement in oxygen resistance or mechanical properties compared to the untreated sample, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Structural metallic materials for applications at high temperatures must have a balance of mechanical properties and oxidation resistance. Coated and internally cooled Ni-based superalloys are used in gas turbine engines close to their high temperature limit, which is imposed by the melting temperature of Ni. The search for new alloys with similar or better capabilities at higher temperatures has concentrated on Nb-silicide based alloys that have lower densities, significantly higher solidus temperatures in excess of 1900 °C and can offer notable mechanical properties []. For example, some of these alloys can have compressive yield strength of about 1800 MPa at room temperature, 1200 MPa at 1000 °C and 500 MPa at 1200 °C []. The oxidation resistance of Nb-silicide based alloys was improved dramatically when the key alloying elements Al, Cr, Si, and Ti were in synergy with other transition and refractory metals, for example Hf, Mo, and simple metal and metalloid elements, e.g., Sn [,,,,]. The equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy was chosen to analyze the effect of each constituent elemental by the subtraction method and, thus, HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi were studied. Among these alloys, HfMoNbTaTi has the best mechanical performance, that is, 27% compressive strain at room temperature and yield strength 367 MPa at 1400 °C. HfMoNbTaTi has great potential for elevated-temperature applications. As the alloy system does not contain very expensive elements such as Re and Ru, it is cost competitive for high-temperature applications like Nb-Hf-Ti alloys in space vehicles. Further modification of composition and/or anti-oxidation coatings are still required for high-temperature applications in the air. According to the experiment results, the effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on mechanical properties of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys were described. For higher room-temperature strength, one should add an element which interacts frequently with the alloy, such as Mo. cited_evidence.text: During the oxidation process, the diffusion of Al and Cr plays a key role, and the slow diffusion may also be partly responsible for the apparent stability of HEA []. The high temperature causes a slow and steady diffusion of Al and Cr elements from the matrix to the surface of the oxide scale, and then reacts with oxygen to form oxides.
